Let

\[
A=\mathbb{C}[x,y], \qquad \mathfrak m=(x,y), \qquad 
I=(y^2-x^7,\; y^5-x^3),
\]

and consider

\[
R=A_{\mathfrak m}/I A_{\mathfrak m}.
\]

We work inside the local ring \(A_{\mathfrak m}\).

First compute the combination

\[
y^3(y^2-x^7)-(y^5-x^3)
= y^5-x^7y^3-y^5+x^3
= x^3(1-x^4y^3).
\]

In the local ring \(A_{\mathfrak m}\), the element \(x^4y^3\) lies in \(\mathfrak m\), so

\[
1-x^4y^3
\]

is a unit. Hence

\[
x^3 \in I A_{\mathfrak m}.
\]

Now using \(y^2-x^7 \in I A_{\mathfrak m}\), we get

\[
y^2=x^7+(y^2-x^7)=x^4x^3+(y^2-x^7)\in I A_{\mathfrak m}.
\]

Thus

\[
(x^3,y^2)\subseteq I A_{\mathfrak m}.
\]

But

\[
\mathfrak m^4 \subseteq (x^3,y^2),
\]

because every monomial \(x^a y^b\) with \(a+b\ge 4\) is divisible either by \(x^3\) or by \(y^2\). Therefore

\[
\mathfrak m^4 A_{\mathfrak m}\subseteq I A_{\mathfrak m}.
\]

So in the quotient ring \(R\), the maximal ideal \(\overline{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m A_{\mathfrak m}/I A_{\mathfrak m}\) satisfies

\[
\overline{\mathfrak m}^{\,4}=0.
\]

Thus the maximal ideal of the local ring \(R\) is nilpotent. A local Noetherian ring with nilpotent maximal ideal has only one prime ideal, namely its maximal ideal. Therefore its Krull dimension is \(0\).

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
